items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So now - we had five children when we moved here, and then we had one more in Connecticut that isn’t a Californian, Matthew.

ctx.x: . . . Irving Townsend said, “I am going to be head of Columbia on the West Coast, so I am leaving my house. It would be a great place for you to live while you’re out here for a year.” It was a great place, right here in Wilton. We found our property where we are and decided to build here and to live here. I can’t believe Iola, that’s fourth generation California, and I’m second at least, maybe more, California – and I wanted all of our kids born in California. If we were on tour, I’d say to Iola, “Go home.” So…

Let me focus on 1971. Columbia starts going through turmoil. They’re changing their roster. They’re moving away from a lot of the jazz acts, and your contract is terminated at that point. How did that happen? What were your reactions? Why did that happen?

items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001
items.q: There’s a recording, just came out last week in England with four of our sons and the London Symphony Orchestra.

ctx.x: Maybe I can just wrap up and ask about your sons’ careers. They seem to be going well.

Oh yeah. There’s a recording, just came out last week in England with four of our sons and the London Symphony Orchestra. So we’ve got the test pressing upstairs. And I’m pleased with it. It was for my 80th birthday. When I was 70 they brought the four sons, when I was 75, the four sons, 80. They bring them from all over the world, because Darius is in South Africa, and Danny and Matthew are in California. Chris is a mile or so from here. And we have a big party in England on my birthday. So this recording has a…
Wanted to give credit where it’s due, huh?
